title: South Asian Spring Awakening #springawakening #springawakeningmusical...
transcript: Fitting that I attended this South Asian production of Spring Awakening during basically a monsoon. The 20-year-old rock musical about sensuality, safety, and shame feels as potent as ever, and staging it through a South Asian lens highlights its timelessness and boundlessness. On the surface, you see the Asian influence in the production design, but there are also some subtleties in the performances that allude to South Asian culture and deepen the themes of the piece. Everyone knows Spring Awakening has a score full of bangers, and thankfully, this cast brings the vocals. I gotta say, though, for how intimate the venue is, I don't understand why it was sometimes so hard to hear the actors and how the mixing was so spotty — I was glad to have been familiar with the piece already. I also felt the show occasionally struggled with conveying the more serious moments, though it greatly excelled in the comedic ones. Salwa Khan and Anil Joseph, who play every adult character, ground the piece wonderfully, representing a spectrum of care through ambivalence to disapproval toward these adolescents, most of whom desperately wish to please their traditional Asian parents. This “Monsoon Awakening” is running through September 6th. With that, another program for my collection.
